topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class to the final lecture of the course and sets out the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard non-targeted treatment modalities, detailing physical resection, radiation, cytotoxic mechanisms of action, and systemic drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies designed to exploit the inherent biological weaknesses of tumor cells, including hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene targeting and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of oncogenic driver kinases alongside the structural mutations and pathway bypasses that cause drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the use of engineered antibodies to target cell surface antigens directly or deliver conjugated cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the immune system's role in cancer control and detail therapeutic strategies such as checkpoint blockade and engineered T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader clinical considerations across cancer treatment, including tumor heterogeneity, early detection, ethical tradeoffs, and future therapeutic strategies.
